Add the speaker's party at the time of each turn

Source: R/context-join.R
add_party.Rd

Adds the party the speaker belonged to on the sitting date of each turn, from the v_party_at_time view.

Usage

add_party(x)

Arguments

x

Turns: a data frame or tibble with a character action_id column, or a lazy table on the package connection (see the Input and output section).

Value

x with the party columns added: a tibble for a data frame, a lazy table for a lazy table.

Details

Three columns are added: party_at_time (the party name), party_id_at_time and party_abbrev_at_time (the party's Abbrev in parties). Stored values are returned unchanged.

get_speeches() output already has party_at_time and party_id_at_time, so only party_abbrev_at_time is added to it.

Input and output

x is a result with one row per turn and a character action_id column, such as the output of get_speeches(), search_speeches_by_terms() or get_sitting_timeline(). It is either a data frame (or tibble), or a lazy table on the package connection, such as one returned with collect = FALSE.

  • A lazy table gets a lazy left join, and nothing is read until you collect() it.

  • A data frame is joined inside DuckDB and returned as a tibble, with the same rows in the same order, its columns first and the added columns after them.

Rows are never dropped or repeated. A turn without a PHID (a presiding officer, or a speaker who is not one member; see get_speeches()), or whose action_id is not in the database, is kept with NA in the added columns. A column that is already in x is not added again: only the missing ones are added, and a message names the ones skipped. If all of them are present, x is returned unchanged.

See also

add_government_status(), get_parties()

Examples

db_connect(sample = TRUE)
turns <- get_sitting_timeline(date = "1918-09-19", chamber = "senate")
add_party(turns)
#> # A tibble: 104 × 14
#>    sitting_id    date       chamber   seq action_id debate_title subdebate_title
#>    <chr>         <date>     <chr>   <int> <chr>     <chr>        <chr>          
#>  1 senate_1918-… 1918-09-19 senate      1 senate_1… N/A          N/A            
#>  2 senate_1918-… 1918-09-19 senate      2 senate_1… ASSENT TO B… N/A            
#>  3 senate_1918-… 1918-09-19 senate      3 senate_1… ASSENT TO B… N/A            
#>  4 senate_1918-… 1918-09-19 senate      4 senate_1… QUESTIONS    POSTMASTER-GEN…
#>  5 senate_1918-… 1918-09-19 senate      5 senate_1… QUESTIONS    POSTMASTER-GEN…
#>  6 senate_1918-… 1918-09-19 senate      6 senate_1… QUESTIONS    RETURNED SOLDI…
#>  7 senate_1918-… 1918-09-19 senate      7 senate_1… QUESTIONS    RETURNED SOLDI…
#>  8 senate_1918-… 1918-09-19 senate      8 senate_1… QUESTIONS    RETURNED SOLDI…
#>  9 senate_1918-… 1918-09-19 senate      9 senate_1… PAPERS       N/A            
#> 10 senate_1918-… 1918-09-19 senate     10 senate_1… PAPERS       N/A            
#> # ℹ 94 more rows
#> # ℹ 7 more variables: action_type <chr>, PHID <chr>, speaker_name <chr>,
#> #   content <chr>, party_id_at_time <int>, party_at_time <chr>,
#> #   party_abbrev_at_time <chr>
db_disconnect()
